title: Wanderer of the Worldlines (Version 1.0.1)
author: Kutsumi Hane
rules:
Doesn't look like a bright morning —

a thin fog lies over the whole town

Before the mirror,

someone is dressing, straightening their clothes

Outside the window, a hush so deep

the butterflies beat their wings — as if they have lost their way

Dizziness strikes

No warning at all

The one at the mirror: no shadow, no trace

Only the butterflies out the window, still beating their wings

…

— Introduction —

This is a series of variant Sudokus.

Every puzzle starts in the same familiar place: a 9×9 grid under standard rules.

Even if you've only dabbled in variant Sudoku, you can jump right in — most puzzles sit comfortably around 2 to 3 stars, with only the final one going a little past 4. All in all, plan for about 10 hours of play.

— Rules —

Sudoku — Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in every row, every column, and every 3×3 box.

Dynamic Fog — Entering a correct digit into a cell will clear the fog from that cell, and perhaps others.

Dynamic Rules —
Selecting a cell may change the rules the puzzle displays.

⚠ To avoid spoilers, refrain from reading the rules when selecting cells still under fog.

All further rules reveal themselves in the game.

Unless explicitly stated, negative constraints do not apply.

— Notes —

-
The series is fully playable on both desktop and mobile.

However, please do not switch devices or browsers mid-series — your progress is saved locally in your browser.

Click the butterfly below to start the first puzzle on
SudokuPad.

And as you go, you'll find your way to the next.

This series was born from a game I played: Sudokuvania, by Skeptical Mario.
The idea took root there and never quite let go of me — until I finally made one of my own.
The grids were set in SudokuMaker, built by sirxemic, and are meant to be solved in SudokuPad, created by Sven Neumann;
The dynamic rules run on a JSON post-processing script, written by cirne. Without their tools, none of this would have taken shape.

And finally — I wish you joyful solving!
